### `discussion_board_admins`

Administrators of the discussion board - This implements the core administrative role management requirement from the requirements analysis. Admins have the highest permissions and can manage users, content, and system configuration. Maintains 3NF by separating admin-specific identity from generic user profiles, allowing future support for role changes, and ensuring that only members with this assignment gain admin authority. For example, assigning 'admin' to a member enables platform management actions. Key relationships: links to user profile for identity, logs role change events, may coordinate with moderation logs. Special behaviors: Admin assignments are auditable, exclusive, and logged.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each admin assignment.
- `discussion_board_user_profile_id`: Linked user profile's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles). Establishes which user has admin rights.
- `assigned_at`: Datetime when admin role assigned - Implements auditability and assignment traceability. Captures when a user becomes admin. Ensures role assignment normalization, example: Member promoted to admin on this timestamp. Cannot be null.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime when admin role was revoked - Implements role transition audit. Null if still active. Example: Admin role revoked during moderation, keeps role history normalized. Null = currently active; else terminated.
- `assigned_by_user_profile_id`: The assigning admin's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) - Ensures traceability of who performed the assignment. For compliance and audit. Example: Assigned by another admin; not null on direct assignment. Behaves as a reference to actor performing change.

### `discussion_board_moderators`

Moderators of the discussion board - Implements the moderator role management requirement. Moderators oversee content, resolve disputes, but do not have full admin privileges. Maintains normalization by separating this role and allowing multiple users to be assigned as moderators, with history for assignment and revocation. For example, granting moderator to a member indicates they can edit/remove posts or manage reports. Key relationships: Links to user profiles; logs assignments. Special behaviors: Moderator assignments are auditable and support periodic review.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the moderator assignment.
- `discussion_board_user_profile_id`: Moderator's user profile [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) - Links moderator to the user.
- `assigned_at`: Datetime moderator role assigned - Tracks when a user became a moderator; supports audit and normalization. Example: Member assigned moderator status at this timestamp. Cannot be null.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime moderator role was revoked; Null if still active. Supports role history normalization. For example: Moderation privileges revoked by admin, timestamped for compliance.
- `assigned_by_user_profile_id`: User profile that assigned moderator (admin or higher moderator) [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) - Ensures assignment is auditable and links to actor.

### `discussion_board_members`

Registered members of the discussion board - Implements core authenticated participant role. Members can create topics, posts, and interact with content. Maintains normalization by having member-specific entry, with relationships to user profiles, and not duplicating data. Example: Only users listed here can author new topics or posts. Key relationships: Linked to user profiles, referenced by posts/comments. Special behaviors: Can be linked to moderation actions and role upgrades/downgrades.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the member assignment.
- `discussion_board_user_profile_id`: Associated user profile's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) - Connects active member entity to user.
- `joined_at`: Datetime user became a member - For onboarding and historical analysis. Strictly normalized: stores only assignment time. Example: Member joined at this date. Not null.
- `left_at`: Datetime user left membership (if left); null if still active. Tracks exits for audit trails. For example: User opts out of platform.

### `discussion_board_guests`

Guests or unauthenticated users - Implements the role of view-only access for guests. Used to audit browse events or personalize some UI per session. Maintains normalization by keeping only atomic session or reference markers, not detailed identity. For example: A guest session is created for analytics, not for authoring. Key relationships: None mandatory, as guests don't own posts. Special behaviors: Entries may be ephemeral or deleted after session expiration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique for each guest session/actor.
- `session_id`: Guest session identifier - Implements non-authenticated session tracking. Ensures normalization by not attributing to a user profile. For example: Tracks which anonymous visitor is browsing. Required, not null.
- `created_at`: Timestamp session created - For analytics and lifecycle management. Ensures guest session data can be expired appropriately. Not null.

### `discussion_board_user_profiles`

User profiles on the board - Implements global user identity, fulfilling profile and authentication requirements. Each profile captures user info such as email, display name, and status, shared by all role-specific tables. Maintains separation from role assignments for strict normalization and identity reusability. For example: A user profile can be assigned roles as member, moderator, admin. Key relationships: Linked to all role tables; referenced by posts and actions site-wide. Special behaviors: Self-service management; deletion anonymizes sensitive data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the user profile.
- `email`: User's unique email address - Implements identification and permission mapping. Must be unique for login and account management. Normalization: Does not duplicate in role tables. Example: alice@example.com. Required.
- `display_name`: User's chosen visible name - For in-platform display, can differ from email or legal name. Ensures separation of personal info and identity. Example: 'Alice W.' Required, not null.
- `registered_at`: Timestamp when profile created - For history, onboarding, and audit. Maintains event normalization. E.g., profile registered at this date. Required.
- `is_active`: Flag if profile is currently active. Implements global enable/disable for security and privacy. E.g., blocked or deleted users are set inactive but preserved for references. Not null.

### `discussion_board_role_changes`

Role assignment and revocation events - Implements full audit trail for all role changes, as required for compliance and traceability. Each change records acting user, affected user, role type, and timestamp. Maintains strict 3NF: Each event is atomic, not duplicative. Example: Promoting a user to moderator is a new record specifying both actors and the action. Key relationships: links user profiles and role objects; referenced by admin review logs. Special behaviors: Immutable, one record per discrete role change event.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies this role change event.
- `target_user_profile_id`: Affected user's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) - Identifies user having role changed.
- `performed_by_user_profile_id`: Acting user's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) - The admin/moderator who invoked the change. Required for traceability.
- `role_type`: Role assigned or revoked (e.g., 'admin', 'moderator', 'member', 'guest') - Implements traceable action record. Only allowed values: admin, moderator, member, guest. Required. Ensures that only valid roles are logged.
- `action_type`: Type of role action ('assigned', 'revoked') - Implements event direction. Allowed values: assigned, revoked. Required. Example: assigned role of moderator, or revoked admin.
- `timestamp`: Datetime when role change occurred - Precise audit. Not null. Example: 2025-07-28T07:52:36.294Z.

### `discussion_board_topics`

Discussion Topic master table – Implements the core requirement from: 'Topic Creation & Threads' (Features), RBAC (Roles & Permissions), and system content structure (Overview & Content Hierarchy). 

Business purpose: Each row represents a unique discussion topic under a specific category. Maintains 3NF by separating topics from posts and categories. For example, this will store the topic title, description, status, and metadata, while posts/replies are stored elsewhere. 

Key relationships: topic snapshots (for audit/versioning), subscriptions (user following), and references to categories and topic creator (user/member/admin). 
Special behaviors: Topics are editable (with version tracking), have status (open/closed/pinned), and are the parent entity for all thread activity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the topic.
- `discussion_board_category_id`: Belonged category's [discussion_board_categories.id](#discussion_board_categories). Links topic to its category, enforcing the topic-categorization structure.
- `created_by_member_id`: Creator's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Identifies which member created the topic (could also be admin/moderator per RBAC).
- `last_edited_by_member_id`: Last editor's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Who last updated the topic (if edited). May be nullable if never edited after creation.
- `title`: Topic title – Implements 'title' aspect (requirement: every topic must have a unique, descriptive title). Clearly identifies the thread at a glance. Ensures normalization by storing only atomic string. Example: '2025 Economic Outlook Regulations'. Required.
- `description`: Topic description – Implements the 'description' requirement (detailed initial statement/problem/agenda for the topic). Preserves normal form by not duplicating post content. Example: 'This thread discusses the impact of fiscal measures on...' Required.
- `status`: Status flag – Implements topic workflow requirement. Business use: distinguishes open, closed, or pinned threads. Example values: 'open', 'closed', 'pinned' (enforced in application). Maintains normalization by not encoding logic in other tables.
- `pinned_at`: Timestamp for when topic was pinned (if applicable). Implements moderation/status history, fulfills auditability. Null if not pinned; updates only when pinned. Maintains atomicity/3NF. Example: 2025-07-28T09:00:00+09:00
- `closed_at`: Timestamp for when topic was closed (if applicable). Fulfills requirement for tracking closure. Null if topic is not closed. Maintains normalization by not aggregating closure data elsewhere.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp – Implements audit trail and recency sorting. Essential for tracking and performance indexes. Required.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp – Enables tracking of edits/changes on the topic. Used for version control and audit log. Required.

### `discussion_board_topic_snapshots`

Topic Snapshot/Audit table – Implements the audit trail and versioning requirement from 'Edit own topics/posts', 'Moderation', and compliance/auditability (Non-Functional, Section 2.5). 

Business purpose: Stores immutable historic versions of each topic for full traceability, rollback, and review by moderators/admins. Maintains 3NF by separating version data from the live topic. For example, when a topic is edited/pinned/closed, a new snapshot record is created.

Key relationships: Back-references the associated topic. Links to the editor and also the original creator.
Special behaviors: Snapshots are strictly append-only; no updates/deletes to preserve true historic record.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique snapshot identifier.
- `discussion_board_topic_id`: Parent topic's [discussion_board_topics.id](#discussion_board_topics). Establishes many-to-one history relationship.
- `edited_by_member_id`: Editor/member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Who performed the edit or action producing this snapshot. Required, always populated in audit trail.
- `title`: Topic title at the time of snapshot. Implements change tracking for titles (requirement: audit logs). Maintains 3NF by separating state history from live record.
- `description`: Topic description at the time of snapshot. Captures content as it was. Maintains normalization; no duplication outside snapshot/audit context.
- `status`: Topic status (open/closed/pinned) at time of snapshot. For rollback/history. Directly supports the versioning requirement.
- `pinned_at`: Pinned timestamp as of this snapshot. Maintains full timeline for audit and rollback. Null if not pinned at that revision.
- `closed_at`: Closed timestamp as of this snapshot. Maintains history for closure events. Null if not closed at that revision.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp. Used for sorting historic timeline. Ensures atomic operation; not inherited from topic.

### `discussion_board_topic_subscriptions`

Topic Subscription table – Implements personalized notifications and topic-following features from 'Notifications & Subscriptions', 'User Journeys', and 'Personalization'.

Business purpose: Records which member users (and possibly moderators/admins) have subscribed to which topics to receive notifications. Maintains full normalization by strictly representing the M:N user-topic subscription with no extraneous data. For example, each row is a single user's subscription to a given topic, supporting fast lookup for notification delivery.

Key relationships: Links member (subscriber) and the topic. May include a subscribe/unsubscribe timestamp for audit/history.
Special behaviors: Unique constraint prevents duplicate subscriptions to the same topic by the same member.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the subscription row.
- `discussion_board_topic_id`: Subscribed topic's [discussion_board_topics.id](#discussion_board_topics). Links subscription to a particular discussion topic.
- `member_id`: Subscribing member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Who is following the topic for notifications. Required.
- `subscribed_at`: Subscription timestamp (when user started following). Implements subscription history/notification logic.
- `unsubscribed_at`: Timestamp for when user unsubscribed, if applicable. Null if still subscribed. Maintains auditability without deleting data.

### `discussion_board_posts`

Discussion Board Post - This implements the posting system requirement from the requirements document, enabling users to submit main topic content or replies. Posts are core user-generated content, backed by rich metadata and normalization. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating attachments, likes, and snapshots into their own models. For example, when a member creates a new reply in a topic, a 'discussion_board_posts' row is created, referencing the topic and user. Key relationships: links to topic, author (member/moderator/admin), snapshot history, attachments, likes. Special behaviors: Posts may be edited, deleted, or moderated; content versioning handled in snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each post.
- `discussion_board_topic_id`: Associated topic's [discussion_board_topics.id](#discussion_board_topics). Links the post to its parent discussion topic or thread.
- `author_member_id`: Author's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Identifies the registered member who created the post; only one required per post.
- `title`: Post title - Implements topic or main reply titling. Describes the subject of the post, shown in previews and search results. Only required for top-level/topic posts. Ensures normalization by storing in the main post entity. For example: 'What are the implications of new tax reforms?'
- `body`: Post content/body - Implements the main content requirement. Holds all user-generated text, supporting rich formatting. Maintains normalization by keeping actual content atomic; attachments, likes, etc., separated. For example: 'The new tax code will likely increase investment...'.
- `is_deleted`: Soft deletion flag - Indicates if this post is deleted or hidden by moderation. Used for non-destructive removal, maintaining audit trails. Abides by normalization by not storing deleted status in snapshots. For example: true if deleted by a moderator.
- `created_at`: Post creation datetime - Captures when the post was created. Ensures traceability and normalization. For example: 2025-07-28T09:52:36+09:00.
- `updated_at`: Post last update datetime - Captures when the post was last modified. Updated on every edit. Maintains normalization for audit. For example: 2025-07-28T10:10:00+09:00.

### `discussion_board_post_snapshots`

Post Snapshot - This implements the versioning/audit requirement from the requirements analysis. Each snapshot records the full content, metadata, and author at a point in time whenever a post is edited. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating version history from the base post entity. For example, editing a post creates a 'discussion_board_post_snapshots' row referencing the post and author. Key relationships: references the post, author identity, and stores all edit versions for review/rollback. Special behaviors: Used for transparency, moderation, and rollback.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this snapshot record.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Parent post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts). Indicates which post this snapshot belongs to. Mandatory for tracking version history.
- `author_member_id`: Snapshot author's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). The user who made this version edit; may differ from original author if moderator/admin edited.
- `snapshot_body`: Snapshot content body - Stores the full text of the post at the edit time. Ensures integrity by archiving true copy at each version. For example, before/after an edit.
- `edit_reason`: Edit reason - Explains why the change was made, supporting moderation transparency. For example: 'Fixed typo', 'Removed prohibited content'.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp - When this version was saved.

### `discussion_board_comments`

Post Comment - This fulfills the comment/in-line feedback requirement: allows users to add targeted comments to specific posts. Maintains normalization by keeping comments as a separate entity, referencing posts. For example, a reply written as a clarification or in-line discussion is a separate 'discussion_board_comments' row, attached to a post and user. Key relationships: references its post, parent comment (for threading), and commenter identity. Special behaviors: Supports nesting/threaded comments via parent_id, soft deletion for moderation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies this comment.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Parent post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts). Indicates which post this comment is attached to.
- `author_member_id`: Commenter's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Member who created this comment.
- `parent_id`: Parent comment's [discussion_board_comments.id](#discussion_board_comments). Enables comment threading. Null for root comments.
- `body`: Comment body - Implements main comment content. Holds atomic plain/rich text. Used in quick replies and clarifications.
- `is_deleted`: Soft deletion flag - Indicates if comment is removed from view while retaining for moderation/audit.
- `created_at`: Comment creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Comment last edit timestamp.

### `discussion_board_post_attachments`

Post Attachment - Implements the file/image upload requirement. Allows users to attach documents, images, or media to posts without embedding content. Maintains normalization by storing attachments separately and only referencing posts. For example, uploading a PDF as evidence creates a 'discussion_board_post_attachments' row linked to a post and uploader. Key relationships: references the post and uploader identity. Special behaviors: Only certain file types/sizes allowed, supports post moderation on attachments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies attachment.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Parent post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts). Indicates which post this attachment is linked to.
- `uploader_member_id`: Uploader's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Member who attached the file/image.
- `file_uri`: File URI - Stores where the attachment is located on disk, CDN, or object storage. Ensures atomized file reference. For example: 'https://cdn.site.com/files/file123.pdf'.
- `file_name`: Displayed file name - User/reader-friendly label for the attachment as shown in UI. Example: 'evidence_chart.pdf'.
- `file_size`: File size (bytes) - Stores the size in bytes for upload constraints and diagnostics.
- `mime_type`: MIME type - Specifies file type for correct rendering and filtering. Example: 'application/pdf', 'image/png'.
- `is_deleted`: Soft deletion flag - Indicates attachment is hidden/restricted without purging from storage (for moderation and audit control).
- `created_at`: Attachment creation timestamp.

### `discussion_board_post_likes`

Post Like - Implements the like/dislike/vote requirement for post feedback and quality surfacing. Each record reflects a user's like/dislike on a post. Maintains normalization by making each like atomic and storing only user + post + flag. For example, when a member likes (or dislikes) a post, a row is created with post ID, member ID, is_like flag. Key relationships: references the post and the member who acted. Special behaviors: Each user can only like/dislike each post once; historical record kept for audit/moderation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this like/dislike record.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Target post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts). Post that received this feedback.
- `author_member_id`: User's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Member who liked/disliked the post.
- `is_like`: Like or dislike flag - true if positive (like/upvote), false if negative (dislike/downvote). Satisfies per-post feedback normalization.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of like/dislike action for audit and analytics.

### `discussion_board_reports`

Discussion Board Report Entity - Implements the requirement for recording all reports submitted by users regarding inappropriate, abusive, or rule-violating content (see moderation and safety requirements). 

This table is central for tracking user-initiated reports across posts, comments, or users. It holds key information about what is reported, by whom, when, and in what context. Maintains 3NF by ensuring each report instance is distinctly identified and all related data are atomic and non-redundant. For example, when a member flags a post for review, a new record is created here with references to the reported object and the report reason.

Key relationships: Each report links to the reporter (user), the content being reported (post, comment, etc.), and the chosen report reason. Tied to action and moderation logs via discussion_board_report_actions and discussion_board_moderation_logs for complete traceability.
Special behaviors: Soft deletion with audit trail, only authorized users (members and above) can create reports, guests cannot.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each report. Implements database integrity and auditability.
- `reporter_id`: Reporter user's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) or equivalent. Links report to the account who initiated it. Ensures traceability and role compliance for moderation.
- `reason_id`: Report reason's [discussion_board_report_reasons.id](#discussion_board_report_reasons). Associates the report with a standardized reason, supporting analytics and moderation flow control.
- `reported_entity_id`: ID of the entity being reported. Supports diverse reportable content types (post, comment, etc.) by storing referred object's unique ID. Maintains normalization by handling just the pointer, not type/state data.
- `reported_entity_type`: Type/category of the reported entity (e.g., post, comment, user). Implements requirement for generic moderation workflows. For example, 'post', 'comment', 'user'.
- `description`: Optional descriptive field where reporter can provide additional context. Maps to moderation requirement for 'reason details', maintaining normalization by being a pure comment.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of report creation. Implements audit/logging requirement for full moderation traceability.
- `resolved`: Indicates if the report has been resolved/closed by moderation. Fulfills process management in moderation workflow. Atomic flag; all status history goes to action/log tables, not duplicated here.

### `discussion_board_report_reasons`

Discussion Board Report Reason Entity - Implements requirement for managing standardized reasons (types) for reporting content (see moderation and analytics requirements).

Purpose is to centralize all predefined (or admin-configurable) reasons available to users when reporting. Maintains highest normalization: one row per unique reason, eliminating redundant/dispersed texts. For example, "Spam", "Harassment", "Off-topic", etc.

Key Relationships: Referenced by multiple reports; never duplicated. Used for moderation analytics (e.g., most common report reasons over time).
Special behaviors: Soft-deletable (if past reports exist), but must not be removed if actively in use.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for report reason; enables safe reference from other tables.
- `reason_text`: Human-readable report reason or label (e.g., 'Spam', 'Harassment'). Implements requirement for user-facing standardized report reason selection. Atomic string, mapped by id.
- `active`: Whether this report reason is currently selectable. Maintains normalization by decoupling reason identity from usage state. For example, old reasons can be deactivated without loss of reference integrity.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the reason was added. Supports analytics, reporting, and admin workflow analysis.

### `discussion_board_report_actions`

Discussion Board Report Action Entity - Implements the requirement for systematically recording action(s) taken in response to each reported item (see moderation workflow and audit compliance).

Each row represents a discrete action (e.g., 'content removed', 'user warned', 'report dismissed') taken by an admin or moderator as part of handling a report. Maintains strict 3NF by separating evented, atomic action records from reports and general activity logs. For instance, if a moderator resolves a report by removing a post, the action is logged here and linked to the report.

Key relationships: References both the original report and the acting admin/moderator. Ties to moderation log for full chain-of-custody.
Special behaviors: Immutable; once created, actions cannot be edited—only new actions may be appended.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the action event. Guarantees atomic, auditable action trails.
- `report_id`: Target report [discussion_board_reports.id](#discussion_board_reports). Links action event to originating report, ensuring full moderation traceability.
- `admin_id`: Admin actor's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). The admin who performed the action, if applicable.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator actor's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators). The moderator who performed the action, if applicable.
- `action_type`: Action taken (e.g., 'remove_content', 'warn_user', 'close_report', 'reject_report'). Implements detailed auditing and process mapping. Ensures pure 3NF by storing only atomic action data.
- `action_notes`: Optional field for additional context/details provided by moderator/admin. Fulfills transparency, appeals tracking, and secondary audit requirements. For example: 'Content restored after appeal.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp of action event creation, required for sequential and legal audit trails.

### `discussion_board_moderation_logs`

Discussion Board Moderation Log Entity - Implements logging requirement for all significant moderation events (see audit, compliance, and transparency requirements).

This table is the atomic ledger for all major actions performed by moderators/admins in the course of resolving reports—covers escalations, blockings, content restorations, etc. Enables post-hoc review, appeals process, and legal compliance. Maintains 3NF by only logging the event and pointer to relevant actor(s)/object(s).

Key relationships: Connects moderation actions to reports and actors. Complements report_actions for a full (non-redundant) audit trail.
Special behaviors: Immutable log; may only be appended to, never edited or deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each log entry, guaranteeing a tamper-evident sequence.
- `report_id`: If log relates to a report, pointer to the report [discussion_board_reports.id](#discussion_board_reports). Enables cross-referencing reports and logs for compliance analysis.
- `admin_id`: Admin actor's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). The admin who performed the action, if applicable.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator actor's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators). The moderator who performed the action, if applicable.
- `log_type`: Nature/type of action being logged (e.g., 'block_user', 'remove_content', 'restore_content', 'escalate'). Implements analytic and legal reporting requirements. Maintains normalization by separating event type from other metadata.
- `details`: Optional detailed information surrounding the action (e.g., reason for escalation). Maintains normalization and pure 3NF by not duplicating atomic event data.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of log creation, required for correct event sequencing and compliance.

### `discussion_board_flagged_content`

Discussion Board Flagged Content Entity - Implements automated/user-initiated flagging for content suspected of violating rules (see features and moderation requirements).

Tracks all flagged content distinct from formal reports (e.g., content automatically flagged by filters or flagged but not yet formally reported). Maintains highest normalization by only storing pointers to flagged objects, state, and timestamps. For example, when automated scans detect suspicious keywords in a post, it is listed here for moderator review.

Key Relationships: Links flagged content to responsible admin/moderator (if set), entity flagged, and state. Integrates with full moderation workflow, triggers further reports or actions if necessary.
Special behaviors: Supports automatic and manual entries; cleared entries are archived, not deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each flagged event; core element for all moderation pre-actions.
- `flagged_by_admin_id`: Admin actor's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). Links the flagged event to the admin who initiated the flagging, if applicable.
- `flagged_by_moderator_id`: Moderator actor's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators). Links to the moderator who flagged the entity, if applicable.
- `flagged_entity_id`: ID of the content entity flagged. Supports all content object types via generic pointer (e.g., post, comment, user). Maintains normalization, enables reusability.
- `flagged_entity_type`: Type/category of flagged content (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'user'). Implements multi-entity moderation tracking.
- `flag_type`: Nature of flag event (e.g., 'auto', 'manual', 'duplicate', 'filter'). Supports analytics, workflows. Maintains 3NF by separating event type from context.
- `reason`: Optional reason/trigger for flag (e.g., matched rule, pattern, user flag). Only details not duplicating data in reports/tables, normalized to avoid redundancy.
- `cleared`: Indicates if flagged content has been reviewed and cleared by moderation. Implements workflow state management, supporting analytics without denormalization.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of flagging event creation (by user or system). Core to all audit and workflow analytics.

### `discussion_board_notifications`

Discussion Board Notification Entity - This implements the notification delivery and tracking requirement, allowing users to receive, view, and manage system, moderation, and activity notifications.

Business purpose: Enables targeted, auditable delivery of notifications about board events (e.g., new reply, post liked, report resolved) to individual users. Maintains 3NF by separating notification content from user settings or delivery preferences. For example, when a post is replied to, a notification record is created per recipient.

Key relationships: references specific users (members, moderators, admins ONLY). Optionally links to actions in other domains via IDs from other domains (not duplicated here).
Special behaviors: Each notification is atomic and individually tracked for read/delivered status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each notification record.
- `recipient_user_id`: Recipient's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members), [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators), or [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). References the user who should receive this notification. Relation name: recipient_user. Target model: discussion_board_members (for normalization, one per relation). Ensures referential integrity and notification traceability.
- `type`: Notification type - Category (e.g., 'new_reply', 'topic_mentioned', 'report_update', 'moderator_action', 'system_announcement').
- `content`: Human-readable notification content for display.
- `is_read`: Whether the notification has been marked as read by the recipient.
- `delivered_at`: When the notification was delivered or made available to the client.
- `read_at`: Timestamp of the user reading the notification, or null if unread.

### `discussion_board_user_notification_settings`

User Notification Settings Entity - Implements user account notification preferences as analyzed in requirements.

Business purpose: Allows each user to control which types of notifications they wish to receive (e.g., push, email, only important, or mute certain types). 3NF is maintained by decoupling preferences from actual notifications and user records. Example: a member may mute all report notifications but receive replies.

Key relationships: 1:1 mapping to a user (member, moderator, or admin); stores current settings for notification types. Special: If no settings, system applies defaults.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each settings record.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members), [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators), or [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). Indicates the user for whom these preferences apply. Relation name: notification_settings_user. Target model: discussion_board_members. 1:1 mapping ensures only one settings record per user.
- `receive_email_notifications`: Whether to receive notifications via email.
- `receive_push_notifications`: Whether to send push/mobile notifications.
- `mute_types`: Comma-separated list of notification types the user chooses to mute (e.g., 'like,report_mention'), null for none.

### `discussion_board_audit_trails`

Audit Trail Log – This implements the 'auditing and accountability' requirement from the Non-Functional Requirements and Technical Overview document.

Captures critical, immutable events related to user actions, moderation activity, and sensitive system changes. Maintains 3NF normalization by storing only atomic event details; connects to user, role, or topic via foreign keys where necessary. Ensures a transparent and traceable system for dispute resolution and compliance.

Usage Example: Records every post deletion, role change, login, or moderation intervention along with timestamps and linking actors.

Key relationships: References users (admins, moderators, members), posts, topics as foreign keys and does not duplicate business data.
Special behaviors: Entries are immutable for integrity. Acts as the single source of truth for accountability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each audit log entry.
- `actor_id`: Actor's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) who performed the action. Needed for tracing origin of action.
- `action_type`: Type of action performed (e.g., create, update, delete, login, moderation). Implements the event requirement for audit. Atomic string for action identifier.
- `target_table`: Table/entity affected by the action. Implements target traceability requirement. E.g., 'discussion_board_posts', 'discussion_board_topics'. Maintains normalization by using reference strings, not duplicating schema details.
- `target_id`: ID of entity affected by the action (e.g., post, topic, user). Business meaning: enables precise accountability without duplication.
- `details`: Textual description giving context to the event, such as before/after values or moderator rationale. Maintains normalization by being strictly contextual. For example, 'Changed topic status from open to closed.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the audit entry was created. Implements chronological trace for auditing. Required for all logs.

### `discussion_board_action_histories`

Action History Log – Fulfils the need for chronological, user-level action histories referenced in the Non-Functional Requirements. Stores a complete timeline of meaningful, non-sensitive user actions for usability and behavior analytics. 3NF compliance is preserved through separation from business entities, with references handled through foreign keys.

Usage Example: Shows the last 100 actions taken by a moderator or tracks a member's contribution over time. Enables better support and dispute resolution.

Key relationships: Links to user ([discussion_board_user_profiles](#discussion_board_user_profiles)), references target table/entity, and preserves event sequences with timestamps.
Special behaviors: Not immutable; can be pruned/cleaned for storage optimization, but raw business data is never stored here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique action history entry identifier.
- `actor_id`: Actor's [discussion_board_user_profiles.id](#discussion_board_user_profiles) who performed the action. Enables tracing user contributions and behavior analytics.
- `action_type`: Type of user action (e.g., post_created, post_edited, report_submitted, topic_subscribed). Implements requirement for granular activity tracking. Ensures only atomic identifiers are stored.
- `target_table`: Table/entity associated with the action (e.g., 'discussion_board_posts', 'discussion_board_topics', etc). Enables normalized linking to actions. Enforces normalization by reference only.
- `target_id`: ID of the entity acted upon (e.g., the particular topic, post, or report). Atomic linkage, not duplicating main data.
- `summary`: Short textual summary for easy human reading, e.g., 'User flagged post as spam'. Implements quick-read analytic requirement. Maintains normalization by only serving as metadata.
- `occurred_at`: Timestamp when the action occurred. Enables temporal analysis. Required for ordering action history.

operations.specification:
This endpoint retrieves a list of discussion board configurations with search, pagination, and sorting functionality. It is based on the discussion_board_configurations Prisma table, which stores system-level global settings, feature toggles, and policy enforcement such as max attachment size, maintenance mode, and welcome messages. The endpoint returns atomic details of each configuration (id, key, value, description, created_at, updated_at), supporting 3NF and operational transparency. Cross-referenced in service initialization and system UIs for settings review. Sensitive modification requires admin endpoint usage. No direct relations, as configs are system-wide and not user-specific.
This operation supports optional search queries (key or description), pagination (page number/size), and sorting (created_at, key, etc.), to enable efficient management even with large numbers of configuration flags. Returned data is never mutated here (read-only list). No authentication required unless sensitive settings are to be exposed, in which case a stricter endpoint may be used.
On error, returns a standard error object with message and reason for failure (e.g., bad page range). If no configs exist, returns an empty data array.

Each configuration contains an id (UUID), key (string), value (string), description (optional string), and timestamps (created_at, updated_at). Authorization is not required unless accessing sensitive fields; in that case, use the admin-prefixed endpoint. The configuration key is unique. This endpoint should be used for operational audits, UI display, and runtime checks (non-mutating read access). No user-related ownership or deletion logic applies, as these are system records. If available, search parameters can filter by key or description using full text. Sorting and pagination parameters—such as page/size, sort_field—should be supported if provided in the request body. Returns an array of objects with full configuration details.
If the database contains no records, an empty array is returned. Errors or invalid queries result in a descriptive message. Does not expose any privileged mutations or sensitive raw values unless role-based control is applied elsewhere.

operations.description:
This API operation allows an administrator to record a new action history entry within the discussion board system. The purpose is to create a chronological, user-level log representing non-sensitive actions, supporting analytics, usability tracking, and dispute resolution. The payload must only reference fields present in the Prisma schema: id (auto-generated), actor_id (user profile ID of initiator), action_type (nature of user action, e.g., 'post_created'), target_table (the logical DB entity affected), target_id (UUID of the target record), summary (optional brief text), and occurred_at (timestamp).

Security: Only admin users are permitted to call this endpoint. The operation must not permit fields not listed in the Prisma schema—DO NOT reference or invent properties such as deleted_at or updated_by. If a request is missing a required field, the API must reject the request.

Business logic: Each action must be atomic (one entry per real-world event) and auditable, supporting later analysis. This endpoint is part of a comprehensive logging and analytics suite for system administrators. No soft or hard delete applies to this entity. Related endpoints include PATCH for search and GET for details.

file_name.description:

Prisma 스키마의 file_name 칼럼 참고.

file_size.description:
첨부파일의 크기(단위: 바이트)입니다. 업로드 제한, 진단, 표시 목적에 사용됩니다. 예시: 204800(200KB)

Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments.file_size 칼럼.

mime_type.description:
파일의 MIME 타입입니다. 예시: application/pdf, image/png 등. 파일 렌더링과 필터링에 꼭 필요합니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments.mime_type 칼럼.

is_deleted.description:
이 첨부파일의 소프트 삭제 여부를 나타냅니다. true이면 UI나 기본 조회에서 제외합니다. 비즈니스 감사 및 실제 삭제/복구 정책 적용 시 사용됩니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments.is_deleted 칼럼 참조.

created_at.description:
첨부파일 레코드가 생성된 타임스탬프입니다. 감사, 정렬, 관리 용도로 활용됩니다.

Prisma file의 created_at 칼럼 설명과 일치.

IDiscussionBoardPostAttachment.description:
게시글 첨부파일 엔터티 객체입니다. 첨부파일의 메타데이터와 업로더, 실제 파일 위치, 파일명, 파일 타입, 업로드 일자, 논리적 삭제 여부 등을 포함합니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments 테이블 구조 및 자세한 칼럼 주석을 기반으로 하며, 모든 필수 정보를 포괄합니다.

discussion_board_post_id.description:
이 첨부파일이 연결될 포스트의 UUID입니다. UI/서버상에서 반드시 존재하는 게시글의 id여야만 하며, 외래키 참조 무결성을 만족해야 합니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments.discussion_board_post_id 칼럼 참고.

file_uri.description:
저장된 첨부파일의 실제 위치(URI)입니다. 업로드 완료 후 파일 서버/스토리지의 경로를 입력해야 하며, 보통 시스템 또는 미들웨어에서 생성됨.

Prisma file_uri 필드 기준.

file_name.description:
UI/사용자에게 보이는 파일명입니다. 업로드 시, 사용자가 직접 명명하거나 브라우저/OS에서 추출된 이름이 될 수 있음.

Prisma 스키마 file_name 설명.

file_size.description:
첨부파일 크기(바이트 단위)입니다. 업로드 정책 및 제한/감사에 사용.

Prisma의 file_size 칼럼 기반.

mime_type.description:
첨부파일의 MIME 타입. 서버 또는 클라이언트가 자동 판별하는 경우도 있음. 예시: image/png, application/pdf 등 사용 권장.

Prisma 스키마 mime_type column 참조.

IDiscussionBoardPostAttachment.ICreate.description:
게시글에 첨부파일을 업로드/등록할 때 사용되는 생성용 타입입니다. 업로더(본인 인증)는 컨트롤러 인증 정보에서 추출하며, 클라이언트에서는 직접 업로더를 지정하지 않습니다.

RBAC상의 보안 원칙과 Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments 모델 주석에 따라, 업로더 식별자는 별도 서버 인증 컨텍스트에서 가져와야 하므로 요청 타입에는 포함되지 않습니다.

file_name.description: 수정할 경우 새 이름을 입력합니다. 사용자 편의성 및 파일명 정정 지원용.

mime_type.description: 첨부파일 MIME 타입을 변경 시 입력합니다. 일반적으론 변경 필요 없음.

is_deleted.description:
첨부파일의 소프트 삭제 여부를 나타냅니다. 삭제 처리 시 true로 전달합니다.

deleted_at과 같은 하드삭제 칼럼이 없으므로, 실제로 삭제하고자 할 경우 true로 세팅만 하고 파일은 남겨 둡니다.

IDiscussionBoardPostAttachment.IUpdate.description:
첨부파일의 부분 정보 수정(메타데이터 편집, 소프트 삭제 등)에 사용하는 객체입니다. 파일 실제 데이터의 업데이트는 지원하지 않으며, 오직 파일명/타입/논리적 삭제 플래그만 변경 가능합니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_attachments 모델 구조 및 보안 정책을 반영합니다.

discussion_board_post_id.description: 조회/필터링할 게시글의 UUID입니다. 이 필드를 이용해 특정 게시글에 대한 좋아요/싫어요 기록만 조회할 수 있음.

author_member_id.description: 특정 회원이 남긴 좋아요/싫어요 데이터를 필터링할 때 사용.

created_at_from.description: 이 시점 이후에 생성된 좋아요/싫어요만 검색. 기간 조건에 활용.

created_at_to.description: 이 시점 이전에 생성된 좋아요/싫어요만 포함. 기간 조건.

limit.description: 페이지당 반환 객체 수. 기본값 100(권장값)

IDiscussionBoardPostLike.IRequest.description:
게시글 좋아요/싫어요 검색 및 필터링, 페이징에 사용하는 쿼리 파라미터 객체입니다. 페이징(페이지/개수), 기간 필터, 다양한 조합의 검색이 가능합니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_likes 관련 비즈니스 요구 및 데이터 기준.

data.description: 실제 페이지에 포함된 좋아요/싫어요 각 엔티티 배열

IPageDiscussionBoardPostLike.description:
좋아요/싫어요 페이징 결과 컨테이너 객체. 페이지 정보와 실제 리스트 데이터가 포함됨.

IPage<T> Type 기반. pagination은 전체 개수/페이지 번호/페이지별 개수 등 포함.

id.description: 엔티티 고유 식별자. UUID. discussion_board_post_likes.id 필드를 나타냄.

discussion_board_post_id.description:
좋아요/싫어요가 속한 게시글의 UUID 참조값입니다.

Prisma discussion_board_post_likes.discussion_board_post_id 칼럼.

author_member_id.description:
좋아요/싫어요 남긴 회원의 UUID 식별자.

Prisma discussion_board_post_likes.author_member_id 칼럼.

is_like.description:
true=좋아요(Upvote), false=싫어요(Downvote) 구분 값.

Prisma is_like 데이터와 일치하게 반환.

created_at.description: 좋아요/싫어요 생성 시각. audit 및 통계에 사용.

IDiscussionBoardPostLike.description:
게시글의 좋아요(혹은 싫어요) 한 건을 표준화한 엔터티 객체. 

Prisma discussion_board_post_likes 모든 실 칼럼을 상세 문서화합니다. 보안상 패스워드 등 민감 정보는 포함되지 않습니다.

discussion_board_post_id.description: 좋아요 혹은 싫어요 대상이 되는 게시글의 UUID입니다.

IDiscussionBoardPostLike.ICreate.description:
좋아요/싫어요(Upvote/Downvote) 액션 등록 요청 타입. 게시글 id와 평가 값만을 받으며, 실제 actor(member)는 인증 컨텍스트에서 자동 주입됩니다.

Prisma 보안 설명에 따라, actor_member_id를 클라이언트가 입력하지 않음에 유의.

is_like.description: 좋아요/싫어요 상태를 전환할 때 사용하는 값.

IDiscussionBoardPostLike.IUpdate.description:
기존 좋아요/싫어요 값(is_like)만을 업데이트합니다. 나머지 필드는 변경 불가.

Prisma discussion_board_post_likes 모델 정책 기준.

resolved.description:
해결 여부로 보고서를 필터링하는 데 사용합니다.

예: resolved=true이면 완료된(처리가 끝난) 신고만, false이면 아직 미처리된 신고만 반환.

reporter_id.description: 신고를 제출한 회원의 UUID로서, 특정 사용자가 제출한 신고만 필터링할 수 있습니다.

reason_id.description: 신고 사유 id(사전 정의)로 필터할 때 사용합니다.

reported_entity_type.description:
신고의 대상 유형(예: post, comment, user 등).

비즈니스 정책에 따라 허용되는 문자열만 입력 권장. Enum으로 관리되면 enum schema로 분리 필요.

limit.description: 페이지 당 반환 엔티티 수(기본 100)

IDiscussionBoardReport.IRequest.description:
신고(Report) 리스트/검색/통계/페이징에 사용하는 요청 파라미터 객체입니다. 다양한 조건(해결상태, 작성자, 사유, 신고대상, 생성일)을 복합 제공.

discussion_board_reports 테이블 실 구조와 활용 시나리오를 문서화함.

IPageIDiscussionBoardReport.description:
신고(Report) 페이징 결과 컨테이너. 페이지 정보와 실제 엔티티 배열이 포함됨.

IPage 표준 구조에 기반함.

id.description: 고유 신고 식별자(UUID). discussion_board_reports.id 컬럼이며, 모든 신고 트래킹의 기본값.

reporter_id.description: 신고한 회원의 고유 UUID 식별자. Prisma reporter_id 컬럼에 해당. 신고 생성 시 인증된 회원만 가능합니다.

reason_id.description:
사전 정의된 신고 사유의 UUID. discussion_board_report_reasons.id와 1:N 참조 관계.

실제 사유(텍스트)는 별도 테이블에서 관리되므로 이 값만 저장됩니다.

reported_entity_id.description: 신고된 대상 Entity의 UUID입니다. 게시글, 댓글, 사용자 등 대상 종류에 맞는 UUID가 저장됨.

reported_entity_type.description: 신고 대상 유형(예: post, comment, user 등). 정확한 Enum 값 혹은 도메인 별로 허용된 값만 사용합니다.

oneOf.description:
신고자가 남긴 부가 설명(선택). 문제 설명, 추가 사유 등. null일 수 있습니다.

Prisma discussion_board_reports.description 칼럼과 일치.

created_at.description: 신고가 제출된 시각. 감사, 통계, 필터링 등에 활용.

resolved.description:

IDiscussionBoardReport.description:
신고(Report) 엔터티 객체. 신고의 상세 내역, 사유, 대상, 처리상태를 모두 포함하여, Prisma discussion_board_reports 설계 및 비즈니스 흐름과 100% 일치.

비밀번호, 토큰, 내부 시스템값 등 민감정보 미포함.

reason_id.description: 신고 사유(프리셋) UUID입니다. 보고서 생성 시 필수.
